candidates.excerpt: WASHINGTON — The U.S. Army Transportation Command has introduced national security as an issue for the Surface Transportation Board to consider as part of its review of the Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern merger proposal, saying that service disruptions following earlier mergers have reduced the nation’s defense readiness. In a filing yesterday (Nov. 17), the Army Transportation Command, or ARTRANS, notes that UP and NS operate approximately 17,600 miles of the 41,000-mile Strategic Rail Corridor Network (STRACNET) and Defense Connector System. They also serve more than 60 defense installations that generate thousands of military-related carloads annually. While not taking a position on the merger, ARTRANS says its filing is intended to make sure the board and others understand the defense-related issues that should be evaluated during the merger proceeding. candidates.title: Port of Savannah container volumes surge 25% in October
candidates.excerpt: The Port of Savannah handled 565,366 TEUs in October 2026, an increase of 25% compared with the same month last year, according to the Georgia Ports Authority (GPA). The result marked the second-highest monthly container volume in the port’s history, supported by strong consumer demand and an extended peak shipping season. Container throughput for fiscal year 2027 to date increased by 7.8%, representing an additional 152,991 TEUs compared with the corresponding period a year earlier. Vessel traffic also increased, with Savannah handling 160 ships during October, up 5% year-on-year. “Our container volumes are driven by strong consumer spending, an extended peak shipping season and our port and inland infrastructure ease of use,” said Griff Lynch, CEO, Georgia Ports Authority. candidates.title: CMA CGM and Royal Railway plan new logistics hub in Cambodia
candidates.excerpt: CMA CGM Group and Cambodia’s Royal Railway have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to develop a rail-connected logistics platform in Phnom Penh. The proposed facility aims to improve container movements between Cambodia’s industrial and commercial centres and international shipping networks, particularly through the Port of Sihanoukville. The agreement outlines plans to combine rail, road and maritime transport within an integrated logistics platform. The project remains at the planning and feasibility stage, with no construction timetable announced. Proposed hub to include container and rail facilities The planned development would include a dry port, container-handling yard, empty container depot and container freight station (CFS). It would also provide rail-connected container-handling facilities, allowing cargo to move between inland logistics operations and the Port of Sihanoukville. candidates.title: DP World reports 50,000 tonnes of avoided emissions through Southampton rail scheme
candidates.excerpt: DP World says its Modal Shift Programme at Southampton has helped avoid an estimated 50,000 tonnes of CO₂ equivalent emissions since its launch in 2023, as more imported containers move inland by rail rather than road. According to the company, the programme has supported the movement of more than 220,000 additional containers by rail, avoiding an estimated 18 million miles of road transport over the past three years. The initiative uses financial incentives to encourage cargo owners to choose rail for inland container movements from DP World Southampton. The company reported that rail’s share of container movements at the port increased from 21% when the programme began to 29% in its latest update. DP World also attributed the introduction of five rail services linking Southampton with Birmingham, Cardiff, East Midlands Gateway, Doncaster and Northampton partly to the programme. candidates.title: Offen firms up four-ship boxship comeback in China
candidates.excerpt: German tonnage provider Claus-Peter Offen has reportedly firmed up all four of its planned 7,000 teu containership newbuildings, ending a nearly two-decade absence from the ordering market. Shipbuilding sources say the Hamburg-based owner has committed to the full quartet after initially signing a letter of intent in September for two firm vessels and two options. China’s Guangzhou Shipyard International (GSI), part of state-owned CSSC, remains linked to the deal, although the builder has yet to be formally confirmed. No contract price or firm delivery dates have emerged, with earlier market reports pointing to slots around 2030. The conventionally powered ships would add around 28,000 teu to Offen’s fleet and mark its first containership orders since 2007. Market sources have also suggested that the four vessels have secured charter backing from one of the world’s ten largest liner operators. candidates.title: ZCG appoints global head of capital formation
candidates.excerpt: ZCG appoints global head of capital formation Z Capital Group (ZCG) has appointed Pierre Garnier as managing director and global head of capital formation. He will lead the firm’s global fundraising and investor relations activities, focusing on strengthening existing investor relationships and developing new partnerships across institutional and private wealth channels. He joins ZCG from Greenstone Equity Partners, where he was director and deputy head of investor relations, supporting fundraising for private markets funds and separately managed accounts. East Broad Top gas-electric car M-1 turns 100
candidates.excerpt: ROCKHILL FURNACE, Pa. — To mark the 100th anniversary of the East Broad Top Railroad’s M-1 gas-electric car, EBT is offering a series of trips on the car Dec. 12-13, touring the entire 7 miles of restored main line. It will be almost 100 years to the day since the self-propelled car made its first trial runs on Dec. 14, 1926. EBT, like many railroads in the ’teens and 1920s, sought a way to cut passenger train expenses in the face of rising competition from private automobiles on a growing network of all-weather, publicly funded highways. EBT has scheduled four M-1 trips each day on Dec. 12-13. Each will cover the traditional tourist-era run 4½ miles north to Colgate Grove, as well as 2½ miles of newly reopened track south to Pogue. The latter is part of the “March to Saltillo” project to reopen more of the 33-mile main line to the semibituminous coalfields around Robertsdale, Pa., that were the reason for EBT’s existence.
